The operator's own explicit instruction for this situation was that persona resolution must be an injected dependency, never hardcoded, fabricated, or guessed.
observedFailure: Not an observed runtime defect — a milestone-scoped, additive build item. The gap was that no seed/demo script existed for the three-party Use Case Zero scenario at all, and the build item's own brief inaccurately described one of the real chain functions (composeUnderwritingAdmissionEvidence) as pure when it is not (see rootCauses).
rootCauses: The brief's own paraphrase called composeUnderwritingAdmissionEvidence one of 'the REAL pure compose functions' in the chain. Reading services/vela/velaUnderwritingAdmissionEvidence.ts in full shows it is async, takes a live Supabase admin client as its first parameter, and performs a genuine read against aegis_assessments/aegis_findings before it can honestly resolve ADMITTED/REFUSED/UNRESOLVED — it structurally cannot be pure.

No prior build item in this chain needed to compose ALL of Factor selection + Aegis admission + disclosure authorization + party bindings + frozen envelope in one seeded, idempotent, reseeding-safe operation — each prior item built and tested exactly one artifact/receipt type in isolation.

No prior script in this repo needed to inject BOTH a full persona triple AND an already-resolved Aegis admission-evidence object as dependencies of one pure composition function — the closest precedent (scripts/vela-slice2e-live-composition.ts) injects only cryptographic keys, not a chain of upstream constitutional evidence.
